newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES DROP BELOW 1,500PTS IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES DROP BELOW 1,500PTS IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Greek stocks drifted below 1,500 points in scant trading on Thursday with investors remaining sidelined in the face of press reports that small brokers were facing liquidity problems.
"Investors are idling until the smoke around the liquidity problems of small brokers clears," said Dimitrios Parashou, fund manager at Vergina mutual funds.

"But the whole issue has been taken out of proportions because it concerns the operations of small brokers with limited retail clientele," he added. "This event does not take the market off its course which is affected positively by long-term improvement in the macroeconomy and the corporate sector."
Greece's tax authorities are reportedly looking into these cases but no official statement has been issued yet.
"I firmly believe that the market will come out stronger of this hiccup just as the late 1996 incident that involved Delta Securities boiled into this year's rally," he said.
Fund managers said prospects for equity investments remained favourable despite temporary blips in short-term rates and inflation.
"There are excellent prospects for Greek stocks in view of lower long-term interest rates and consumer price inflation," Parashou said.
"The rise in short-term rates and the resurgence of CPI inflation in June reflect temporary conditions, not a permanent change in fundamentals," he added.
June CPI inflation, expected to be officially released on Friday, was seen rising to around 5.5 - 5.6 percent from 5.4 percent in May, a government source told Reuters.
The Athens general index drifted 0.67 percent or 10.06 points lower to 1,493.53 from Wednesday's 1,503.59, recovering from an intra-day low of 1,478.92 recorded at mid-session.
Industrials edged 0.22 percent forward, providing considerable support to the market which was led lower by banks, down 1.45 percent, and construction, 1.57 percent.
Turnover amounted to 9.7 billion drachmas on volume of 2.6 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 149 to 58 with 20 shares unchanged on 227 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.30-$11.75. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,114-1,144 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,119-1,179 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument firmed 15 drachmas to 6,385.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 554.07-589.43 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $62.16-$64.81. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,898-3,109 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $8.92-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 178-207 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
